candidates.change_summary: Record block.number instead of block.number + 1 as the guess block.
Record block.number + 2 instead of block.number + 1 as the guess block.
Remove the guard preventing re-locking an existing guess, allowing callers to overwrite their guess.
Remove the 1 ether payment requirement from lockInGuess.
Remove the assignment storing the caller's guess hash, leaving the stored guess as zero.
Delete the statement resetting guesses[msg.sender].block to 0, so the same guess remains locked and settle can behave differently on subsequent calls.

Replace the strict inequality check with `block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block`, allowing settle to be called one block earlier (when the blockhash is still zero), changing revert/success timing and settlement outcome.
Replace the equality comparison of the guess with inequality (`!=`), inverting the payout condition so the winner now loses and losers win.
Delete the guard requiring that no guess is already locked in, allowing repeated lockInGuess calls to overwrite an existing guess.
Change the msg.value requirement from 1 ether to 2 ether, so calls with 1 ether now revert instead of storing a guess.
Store block.number + 2 as the target block instead of block.number + 1, changing which block hash the guess is checked against.
Store the negated hash (via NOT) instead of hash as the guess, so settle() compares against a different value.
